topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's focus on cancer evolution, the microenvironment, and the Darwinian model of tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Clonal selection and epigenetic mechanisms in tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells acquire competitive fitness advantages through sequential genetic mutations and transient epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and cell of origin in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell model and present experimental evidence from leukemias and intestinal adenomas identifying which cell types initiate malignancies.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, inflammation, and stromal dependence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promotional stimuli, inflammatory signaling, and supportive stroma permit and sustain tumor progression.

topics.label: Methods for investigating tumor evolution and spatial architecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the experimental and computational tools used to map mutational timing, cell plasticity, and microenvironmental interactions in tumors.

topics.label: Comprehensive synthesis of cancer evolutionary dynamics
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the lecture's core concepts by integrating mutational accumulation, cell-of-origin traits, and microenvironmental pressures into an overall evolutionary model.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of the next session
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
